description.short_caption: Axial and coronal CT images showing diffuse colonic mural thickening in the ascending and transverse colon.
description.detailed_description: This image consists of axial (left) and coronal (right) reformatted CT images of the abdomen. Both images demonstrate diffuse, long-segment mural thickening of the colonic wall in the residual ascending and transverse colon, as indicated by arrows. The thickened colonic wall appears hypodense relative to the surrounding structures, consistent with inflammatory or infectious colitis. Adjacent fat stranding is also visible, suggesting pericolonic inflammation.
visible_findings: involvement of ascending and transverse colon

description.short_caption: Granulomatous inflammation with fungal elements and Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon.
description.detailed_description: This image shows two histopathology panels stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). Panel A highlights severe granulomatous inflammation with a multinucleated giant cell (indicated by an arrow) engulfing fungal zygospores, which have a thin eosinophilic wall and foamy cytoplasm. Panel B demonstrates broad, infrequently septate fungal hyphae (indicated by an arrow) surrounded by strongly eosinophilic material, consistent with the Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon. Both panels show a background of mixed leukocytic infiltrate, including numerous eosinophils.
visible_findings: multinucleated giant cell engulfing fungal zygospores

description.short_caption: Fungal culture and lactophenol blue preparation showing characteristic fungal morphology.
description.detailed_description: Panel C shows a fungal culture on chloramphenicol Sabouraud dextrose agar with waxy cream-colored colonies exhibiting radiate fissures, surrounded by large mucoid colonies suggestive of enteric contamination. Panel D displays a lactophenol blue preparation of the fungal culture, highlighting characteristic clavate conidia (indicated by arrows) and septate hyphae. The preparation provides detailed visualization of fungal structures under light microscopy.
